sources.entry: ggml - Defines the quantized block formats and the per-ISA dot-product kernels over them that every llama.cpp type rests on.

summary.one_liner: ggml is a plain C/C++ tensor library for machine learning that provides the core tensor operations and quantized formats used by llama.cpp.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes ggml as a simple, portable, and efficient tensor library for machine learning with minimal setup. It is implemented in plain C/C++ without external dependencies and is said to run on x86, ARM, RISC-V, LoongArch, PowerPC, s390x, and WebAssembly. It states that SIMD-optimized kernels exist for x86, ARM, and RISC-V. It supports 2- to 8-bit integer quantization plus MXFP4 and NVFP4 microscaling formats, and it claims zero memory allocations during runtime. The README also mentions broad backend support across CPU, GPU, NPU, and browser. Build is via CMake, and a minimal matrix-multiplication example is pointed to in examples/simple.
use_cases: building a small tensor computation library into a C/C++ project
running machine learning tensor ops on CPU without heavy dependencies
studying a minimal matrix multiplication example
cross-platform inference on ARM, x86, RISC-V, or WebAssembly
notable: SIMD-optimized kernels for x86, ARM, and RISC-V
2- to 8-bit quantization plus MXFP4 and NVFP4 microscaling formats
caveats: Core library changes (including CMake build system) are directed to llama.cpp rather than this repo
README is brief and gives little detail on the API or per-ISA kernel internals
